channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: CoreWeave Sees ‘No Reason’ That Nvidia Partnership Will Change
item.description: CoreWeave Inc. Chief Executive Officer Michael Intrator expressed faith in his company’s relationship with Nvidia Corp., a key backer and supplier that is now engulfed in controversy.
item.dc:creator: Dina Bass

item.title: CoreWeave Boosts Forecast, Easing Slowdown Concerns
item.description: AI computing provider CoreWeave topped analysts’ estimates with quarterly results and boosted its annual forecast, easing investor concerns about the debt-laden business suffering a slowdown. Brody Ford reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Walker & Dunlop CEO on ‘27 Data Center Buildout Outlook
item.description: Willy Walker, Chairman and CEO of Walker & Dunlop, says modest daily interest-rate moves are unlikely to stall commercial real estate activity, though sharp jumps can temporarily halt deals while buyers and sellers reassess asset prices and financing costs. Rate expectations may also prompt some investors to act sooner rather than wait for further increases. Walker speaks with Vonnie Quinn & Jess Menton on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: KPMG Chief Economist Predicts Hot PCE Report After CPI
item.description: Diane Swonk said inflation data running hotter than expected for a third consecutive month showed broad price increases across goods and services, including hotels, airfares, furniture and entertainment; used-car prices were a notable exception. She expects the PCE measure to show even hotter underlying services inflation and said a half-point Fed hike could be considered to bolster the central bank’s credibility. Swonk speaks with Vonnie Quinn & Jess Menton on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Sonos Plans ‘Many’ New Products Next Year to Capitalize on AI Era
item.description: Sonos Inc. reported revenue growth and teased new products as the company looks to establish its signature audio system as an open platform for showcasing artificial intelligence agents throughout the home.
item.dc:creator: Chris Welch

item.title: OpenAI Third-Quarter Revenue Soars Nearly 50% to $10 Billion
item.description: OpenAI’s quarterly revenue hit $10 billion for the first time in the three months ending in September, according to people familiar with the matter, driven by strong demand for its latest artificial intelligence software.
item.dc:creator: Rachel Metz and Rebecca Torrence

item.title: Why Nvidia and Jensen Huang Matter So Much to Markets
item.description: It’s not often that a revelation about a relationship erases a trillion dollars of value from the stock market. But that’s what’s happened in the wake of media reports that a woman suspected of being an asset for Chinese intelligence had grown close to Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang, who acknowledged having an extramarital affair.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Pfeiffer, Ingrid Fuary-Wagner and Wendy Pollack

item.title: Stifel CEO on Anthropic, Integrating AI and Fed Policy
item.description: Stifel CEO and Chairman Ron Kruszewski discusses the firm’s new partnership with Anthropic, announced at Stifel’s 2026 Blueprint Conference in Las Vegas. The tools are intended to help advisers organize work, improve productivity and communicate with clients, not replace human judgment. Speaking on "Bloomberg The Close," Kruszewski also comments on Federal Reserve monetary policy and the state of the market. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Jensen Huang’s 700,000% Return Magnifies Nvidia Succession Risks
item.description: The office of Nvidia’s Jensen Huang has an unusual setup: The chief executive officer sits at an enormous oval desk facing his lieutenants, with room for more employees in stadium seating behind them. The arrangement — created as part of Nvidia’s headquarters in Santa Clara, California — is purpose-built to suit how Huang runs the company. Though it’s not uncommon to see cultlike tech CEOs who obsess over details, Huang is in a class of his own. He has led the business since its very beginning 33 years ago, the longest such run in Silicon Valley. And even as Nvidia grew into one of the world’s most powerful companies — with a stock return of more than 700,000% — there’s still no one designated to potentially replace him. Ian King, Bloomberg News US Semiconductor reporter discusses the latest. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: CoreWeave Earnings Top Estimates, Boosts Annual Forecast
item.description: Gil Luria, D.A Davidson technology research head, says CoreWeave's earnings are "very good," and there's not enough compute power to go around. But he says CoreWeave will have trouble raising "more capital to keep going." He speaks on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Fed's Bowman Warns About Potential Impact of AI Bets Not Panning Out
item.description: Federal Reserve Governor Michelle Bowman says she sees a number of risks to economic activity from financial markets, including a sharp downturn in stock prices if returns on investments in AI fall short of expectations. She speaks at a Council on Foreign Relations event in Washington. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: La crisis de Nvidia expone su dependencia de Jensen Huang
item.description: La junta está investigando si su CEO fue objeto de una espía china y evalúa el riesgo de un futuro sin su singular líder.
item.dc:creator: Ian King

item.title: CoreWeave Quiets Doubts About AI Business With Upbeat Outlook
item.description: CoreWeave Inc. eased fears about its debt-laden business during a high-stakes quarterly report, indicating that sales growth remains strong despite challenges facing the data center industry.
item.dc:creator: Dina Bass and Brody Ford

item.title: Sony Bets on Anime to Become Intellectual Property Giant, Fuel Future Growth
item.description: The PlayStation company looks to a beloved genre to find its next big hit
item.dc:creator: Sohee Kim

item.title: Anthropic Investors Shop IPO Shares Early, and at a Big Premium
item.description: Some Anthropic PBC backers are offering a portion of their IPO allocation to new investors in the run-up to the largest public listing on record.
item.dc:creator: Bailey Lipschultz and Sridhar Natarajan

item.title: US Midterms Fallout, Biggest Heist in History
item.description: "Bloomberg Crypto" covers the people, transactions, and technology shaping the world of decentralized finance. Today's guests: Securitize Chairman, CEO & Co-Founder Carlos Domingo, The Blockchain Association Interim CEO Kristin Smith, AVA Labs Vice President of Onchain Finance Morgan Krupetsky, Ledger Chairman and CEO Pascal Gauthier, and Anchorage Digital Co-Founder & CEO Nathan McCauley. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: PlayStation Cancels Online Shooting Title ‘Fairgames’
item.description: There will be no job cuts alongside the cancellation, Sony said
item.dc:creator: Jason Schreier

item.title: Everybody Will Be Hacked At Some Point: Ledger CEO
item.description: Pascal Gautier, chairman and CEO of Ledger, joins Isabelle Lee and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." The hackers who stole $6.3 billion from Binance last week found a way to take 40% of the stolen cryptocurrency in one hit, reducing their chances of being caught in the act, and it cost them just $15. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia Board Members Tap Wachtell’s Kim for Huang Probe
item.description: Nvidia Corp.’s independent board members tapped a former top federal prosecutor to help probe Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese spy.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Hurtado and Bob Van Voris

item.title: SoftBank Loses $7 Billion After Big US Data Center Writedown
item.description: SoftBank Group Corp. reported its first net loss in almost two years after the tech investor swallowed a $3.7 billion writedown over its US data-center projects and AI valuations dipped around the world.
item.dc:creator: Min Jeong Lee
